title: MeitY's SAMRIDH Programme Supports 5 Startups through Accelerator-led Innovation; ₹1.81 Crore Disbursed under the Programme
body_text:
The Startup Accelerator of MeitY for Product Innovation, Development, and Growth (SAMRIDH) programme, designed to accelerate around 300 Startups through existing and upcoming Accelerators in Health-tech, Ed-tech, Agri-tech, Consumer-tech, Fin-tech, Software as a Service (SaaS) and sustainability sectors. The programme successfully concluded on 31 st January, 2026.
During the last five years, 7 accelerators from the State of Andhra Pradesh submitted Expressions of Interest (EoI) under the SAMRIDH programme. Of these, one accelerator each was from Ananthapuramu, Guntur and West Godavari districts, while four accelerators were from Visakhapatnam district. Out of these, one accelerator, namely Kalpataru Centre of Excellence (CoE) by AIC STPINEXT Initiatives, located in Visakhapatnam district, was selected for implementation of the programme.
Under SAMRIDH programme, MeitY Start-up Hub (MSH) under Digital India Corporation (DIC) monitors and evaluates the performance of selected accelerators based on quantitative and qualitative parameters of the acceleration programme, which also tracks revenue and valuation growth of supported startups on an annual basis.
The SAMRIDH programme provides financial support of ₹2 lakh per startup to selected accelerators, along with matching funding to startups up to a maximum of ₹40 lakh, in accordance with programme guidelines. In Andhra Pradesh, 5 startups were selected and supported through the selected accelerator, Kalpataru Centre of Excellence (CoE), Visakhapatnam. The startups supported are as under:
Selected Accelerator Startups Kalpataru Centre of Excellence (CoE), AIC STPINEXT, Visakhapatnam i. Aerogravity Private Limited ii. Cairovision Private Limited iii. Epsum Labs Private Limited iv. Scraptechies Solutions Private Limited v. Voptimaise Climate Tech Solutions Private Limited
Further, an amount of ₹1.81 Cr was allocated and disbursed to the selected accelerator Kalpataru Centre of Excellence (CoE), AIC STPINEXT, Visakhapatnam.
This information was submitted by Union Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology Shri Jitin Prasada in Rajya Sabha on 07.08.2026.

Vinod Kumar / Kanishk Sharma

enrichment.summary: In a Rajya Sabha reply dated 7 August 2026, MeitY Minister of State Jitin Prasada provided details of the SAMRIDH programme, which aimed to accelerate around 300 startups across sectors like Health-tech, Ed-tech, Agri-tech and Fin-tech, and concluded on 31 January 2026. In Andhra Pradesh, out of 7 accelerators that applied, one accelerator - Kalpataru Centre of Excellence (CoE) by AIC STPINEXT Initiatives, Visakhapatnam - was selected and supported 5 startups, with ₹1.81 crore disbursed to it under the programme.
enrichment.context:
SAMRIDH (Startup Accelerator of MeitY for pRoduct Innovation, Development and growtH) is a flagship scheme of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, implemented through MeitY Startup Hub (MSH) under Digital India Corporation (DIC), aimed at strengthening the software product startup ecosystem in India. It works on an accelerator-led model where MeitY provides funding support to established accelerators (₹2 lakh per startup) who in turn mentor and support early-stage startups, with matching growth funding to startups capped at ₹40 lakh, contingent on the startup raising equal or more matching investment from other sources. This model leverages existing accelerator networks and expertise rather than the government directly funding startups, aiming to improve efficiency and market-readiness of India's software product ecosystem, which is a key focus of the broader Digital India and Startup India initiatives.

The release is significant for illustrating how central government schemes are implemented in a geographically uneven manner - despite multiple districts in Andhra Pradesh submitting expressions of interest, only one accelerator (in Visakhapatnam) was ultimately selected, highlighting the competitive and merit-based selection process under such schemes. This ties into larger governance themes of Centre-State coordination, regional innovation hubs, and the promotion of the digital/technology startup ecosystem as part of India's economic diversification strategy, especially in emerging technology sectors like climate tech, aerospace, and data-driven services represented by the five supported startups.

options: Ministry of Commerce and Industry through Startup India Hub
MeitY Startup Hub (MSH) under Digital India Corporation (DIC)
Department of Science and Technology's Technology Development Board
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, SAMRIDH is monitored and evaluated by MeitY Startup Hub (MSH), which functions under Digital India Corporation (DIC), a MeitY entity.

prelims_questions.question: Under the SAMRIDH programme, what is the maximum matching funding a startup can receive, in addition to the ₹2 lakh support given to the accelerator?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that matching funding to startups is provided up to a maximum of ₹40 lakh, in accordance with programme guidelines, apart from ₹2 lakh per startup given to the selected accelerator.
